definitions.availability_pct: run_time_h / planned_time_h x 100; planned time is 7.5 h per shift and excludes the 0.5 h planned break
definitions.performance_pct: (actual_units / run_time_h) / ideal_rate_uph x 100; not capped, values above 100 can occur when a line beats its nameplate rate
definitions.downtime_by_cause: downtime hours grouped by reason with share of total and cumulative share for Pareto analysis; reason None (stops under 0.1 h) excluded

assumptions: All data is synthetic and generated from a fixed random seed. No real plant, company or measurement is represented.
Each shift is 8 hours with a 0.5 hour planned break. Planned production time is 7.5 hours and the planned break is excluded from every OEE denominator.
Each line runs one product category per shift. Lines A and B mostly run Standard, Line C mostly runs Premium.
Line B is the oldest line and carries roughly 1.5 times the breakdown downtime of the other lines.
A major Line B breakdown occurs in the week of 9 to 15 March 2026.
A plant maintenance programme starts on 1 July 2026 and cuts breakdown downtime by about 35 percent on all lines.
The last three days of each month show a mild planning push with higher planned units.
Cost assumptions are in Malaysian Ringgit (RM), are illustrative only and are never used to claim savings.
Aggregated KPIs use time weighted sums. Row level percentages are never averaged.

scenario.name: Changeover reduction programme (what-if)
scenario.description: Models the effect of cutting changeover downtime by 40 percent and quality stop downtime by 20 percent, with the regained run time converted into units at each row's own production rate. The result is a modelled what-if, not a measured outcome.
assumptions: Changeover downtime reduced 40% via SMED-style standardisation
Quality stops reduced 20% via first-pass checks
